learningObjectives: Explain what a Class is and why it reduces redundancy across TestSheets.
Create a Class using the two primary methods: manual creation and drag-and-drop from an existing Attribute.
Distinguish 'Create Class from Attribute' from 'Create Structure from Attribute'.
Use Resolve Class Reference and the Relevant column/F11 to manage how a Class behaves inside different TestSheets.

elements.description: A reusable Tosca object — conceptually similar to a Library in the TestCase section — that lets you define an Attribute structure (with its Instances and combinations) once and reuse it across many TestSheets via a Class Reference. A typical candidate is data that shows up repeatedly, like a Customer Attribute structure used by every TestSheet that touches customer data.

Reuse saves setup time, and because a Class Reference stays linked to its source Class, updating the Class once propagates that change to every TestSheet referencing it — centralizing maintenance instead of repeating it in every TestSheet.

bulletPoints: Class = define once. Class Reference = reuse anywhere, unlimited times.
Update the Class → every Class Reference updates automatically.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Four ways to create a Class

elements.title: Creation methods
items: Manually — right-click a TestCase Design Folder → 'Create Class', then build Attributes/Instances inside it just like a TestSheet.
Drag & drop an existing Attribute (or Attribute structure) onto a TestCase Design Folder — Tosca creates a Class and automatically converts the original Attribute into a Class Reference.
Extract Class — right-click an entire TestSheet and choose 'Extract Class' to convert its whole structure into a Class, with a Class Reference created in its place.

Drag & drop a Module onto a TestCase Design Folder — the Class takes the Module's name, the Module's Attributes become TestCase Design Attributes, and the Module Attributes' ValueRanges become Instances. This course focuses on methods 1 and 2.

elements.term: Dragging an Attribute WITHOUT top-level combinations
elements.description: If the Attribute structure you drag doesn't already have Instances/combinations at its top level, Tosca asks you to choose: 'Create Class from Attribute' copies the structure AND auto-generates Instance combinations based on the combinations that already existed in the source TestSheet. 'Create Structure from Attribute' copies only the Attribute/Instance structure, with no combinations.

elements.text: A Class Reference is visually distinguished by a white arrow overlay on its icon.

bulletPoints: 4 creation methods exist; this course covers manual creation and drag-and-drop from an Attribute in depth.
Dragging an Attribute with existing top-level combinations converts it directly; dragging one without combinations prompts a Create Class vs Create Structure choice.

elements.description: Once created, a Class can be modified exactly like a TestSheet — add or remove Attributes, create or delete Instances, adjust combinations, and set Character/Position on its Instances.

As with Libraries, if you want to change or remove a Class without affecting the values currently shown in a particular reference, select 'Resolve Class Reference' on that reference first. This breaks the live link, letting that instance of the data be modified or the Class removed independently.

Not every Instance in a Class needs to be used in every TestSheet that references it — Instances not selected in a given Class Reference's combinations are shown bolded in the TestSheet. Separately, whole Attributes inside a Class Reference can be marked irrelevant for a specific TestSheet using the 'Relevant' column (add it via the Column Chooser): unchecking the box for an Attribute grays it out. Press F11 to toggle hiding/revealing these irrelevant Attributes.

bulletPoints: Resolve Class Reference = detach this specific reference from the live Class link before editing/removing the Class.
Bolded Instance = unused in this Reference's combinations. Grayed-out Attribute (via Relevant column, F11 to show/hide) = marked not relevant to this TestSheet.

examPitfalls.title: Editing a Class Reference and expecting it to stay independent
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Changing a value inside a Class Reference and assuming other References to the same Class are unaffected.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A Class Reference stays live-linked to its Class by default — changes to the Class propagate everywhere it's referenced. To make one reference diverge, use 'Resolve Class Reference' on it first.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing 'Create Class from Attribute' with 'Create Structure from Attribute'
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming both options behave identically when converting an Attribute without existing combinations.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: 'Create Class from Attribute' also auto-generates Instance combinations from the source TestSheet's existing combinations. 'Create Structure from Attribute' copies only the Attribute/Instance structure, with no combinations created.

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting 'Extract Class' as a creation method
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Only remembering manual creation and drag-and-drop-from-Attribute as ways to make a Class.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A whole TestSheet can also be converted directly into a Class via right-click → 'Extract Class', which creates a Class Reference in its place — a third method alongside manual creation and dragging an Attribute.

examPitfalls.title: Mixing up bolded Instances with grayed-out Attributes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating 'bolded Instance' and 'irrelevant Attribute (grayed out)' as the same signal.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Bolded = an unused Instance within this Reference's combinations. Grayed-out = a whole Attribute manually marked irrelevant via the Relevant column, toggled with F11. They're separate mechanisms.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester updates the Class 'Customer Data', adding a new Instance. What happens to the TestSheets that already reference this Class?

options.text: Nothing — TestSheets must be manually refreshed one by one.
Each Class Reference automatically reflects the update, showing the newly created Instance.
Existing References break and must be recreated.
Only the first Reference created updates.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the core value proposition of using a Class in the first place.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Class References stay live-linked to their Class. Updating the Class (e.g. adding a new Instance) automatically makes that change visible in every Reference to it, without manual work.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester drags an Attribute with no top-level Instances or combinations onto a TestCase Design Folder and wants Tosca to also generate combinations automatically, based on the source TestSheet's existing combinations. Which option should they choose?
practiceQuiz.hint: One option copies structure only; the other also brings combinations along.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Create Class from Attribute' copies the structure AND auto-generates Instance combinations from what already existed in the source TestSheet. 'Create Structure from Attribute' copies structure only, with no combinations.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to remove a Class entirely, but one particular Class Reference should keep its current values unaffected. What must they do first?

options.text: Delete the Class directly — References always keep a frozen copy automatically.
Select 'Resolve Class Reference' on that specific reference before removing the Class.
Rename the Class instead of deleting it.
Mark the Attribute as BusinessRelevant = No.

practiceQuiz.hint: Same concept as detaching from a Library before removing the shared object.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Resolve Class Reference' breaks the live link between that specific reference and the Class, letting it keep its current values independently — this should be done before removing or heavily changing the source Class.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Class Reference, an entire Attribute (not just one Instance) needs to be excluded from view for a specific TestSheet because it isn't relevant there. How is this done?

options.text: Delete the Attribute from the Class Reference.
Uncheck it in the 'Relevant' column (added via Column Chooser); toggle visibility of irrelevant Attributes with F11.
Mark every Instance under it as Invalid.
This isn't possible — all Attributes in a Class Reference must always be shown.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is a per-Reference visibility setting, not a structural deletion.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Adding the 'Relevant' column via the Column Chooser lets you untick an Attribute to mark it irrelevant for that specific Class Reference (it grays out); F11 toggles whether irrelevant Attributes are hidden or shown.

quickRecap.value: Reusable Attribute structure (like a Library) — define once, use via Class Reference anywhere.
Manual, drag Attribute onto Folder, Extract Class from a TestSheet, drag a Module onto a Folder.

quickRecap.key: Create Class vs Create Structure from Attribute
quickRecap.value: Class = structure + auto-generated combinations. Structure = structure only, no combinations.
Detaches one Reference from the live Class link before editing/removing the Class.
An Instance in the Class not used by this Reference's combinations.
Marks/hides whole Attributes as irrelevant for a specific Class Reference.
